title: OpenAI Q3 Revenue Tops $10 Billion, But Losses Hit $10.9 Billion
summary: OpenAI Q3 revenue hit $10 billion, up 50% from Q2, but operating losses reached $10.9 billion. Loss per dollar fell to $1.09 as Anthropic races ahead.
body_markdown:
OpenAI Earnings


# OpenAI Q3 Revenue Tops $10 Billion, But Losses Hit $10.9 Billion


By OpenTools Team


·


November 12, 2026


OpenAI crossed $10 billion in quarterly revenue for the first time, up 50% from Q2, but its operating loss hit $10.9 billion. The loss‑per‑dollar figure fell to $1.09, even as rival Anthropic posted $17 billion in revenue with a fraction of the losses.


## The $10 Billion Milestone — and the $10.9 Billion Loss


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) generated **$10 billion in revenue** in the three months ended in September, its first quarter at that level, according to[Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-10/openai-third-quarter-revenue-soars-nearly-50-to-10-billion) . Revenue rose about 50% from the second quarter and was nearly three times the year-earlier level. The catch: the company's adjusted operating loss for the same period was **$10.9 billion** , up from $10.1 billion the prior quarter.


The figures were shared with investors on a call Tuesday, where President Greg Brockman and CFO Sarah Friar spoke, according to[Quartz](https://qz.com/openai-revenue-operating-loss-10-billion-third-quarter-111126) . OpenAI declined to comment.


## Loss Per Dollar Falls to $1.09


Behind the headline loss, there's a real efficiency story.[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) lost **$1.09 for every dollar of revenue** in Q3, down from $1.50 three months earlier,[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonmarkman/2026/11/11/openai-revenue-hits-10-billion-in-q3-as-loss-per-dollar-falls-to-109/) reported. Its adjusted operating margin improved to **-109%** from -150% in Q2.


Most of the loss is the cost of buying compute ahead of the revenue it produces. OpenAI has signed massive infrastructure commitments, including a **$300 billion five-year agreement with Oracle** , roughly **$250 billion in[Microsoft Azure](https://opentools.ai/tools/microsoft-azure) purchase commitments** , and a **$38 billion seven-year deal with[Amazon](https://opentools.ai/organizations/amazon) Web Services** , per[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonmarkman/2026/11/11/openai-revenue-hits-10-billion-in-q3-as-loss-per-dollar-falls-to-109/) . Demand exceeds available compute, so added capacity converts to revenue quickly — the question is when the loss curve finally flips.


## Enterprise Is Now Half the Business


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's enterprise revenue **doubled quarter over quarter** and now makes up **50% of total revenue** , making it the largest single source. CFO Sarah Friar attributed the growth to products aimed at builders and developers, telling[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonmarkman/2026/11/11/openai-revenue-hits-10-billion-in-q3-as-loss-per-dollar-falls-to-109/) that the driver is products like Coding and Cyber. Consumer sales rose 20% in the quarter, with subscriptions topping **100 million** and ChatGPT reaching **1.2 billion weekly active users** .


> "What's driving that is products like Coding, Cyber, starting to get more virtual assistants like Dots into the enterprise."


**Sarah Friar** - CFO, OpenAI


## Anthropic Is Ahead — and Far More Efficient


The contrast with[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) is stark. Anthropic posted **roughly $17 billion in Q3 revenue** — nearly $7 billion more than[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) — while its operating loss was just **$567 million** , a fraction of OpenAI's $10.9 billion, according to[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonmarkman/2026/11/11/openai-revenue-hits-10-billion-in-q3-as-loss-per-dollar-falls-to-109/) and[Quartz](https://qz.com/openai-revenue-operating-loss-10-billion-third-quarter-111126) .


Anthropic first surpassed OpenAI in quarterly revenue in Q2 2026, posting **$11.6 billion against OpenAI's $6.7 billion** ,[Quartz](https://qz.com/anthropic-surpasses-openai-revenue-q2-2026-081926) noted. One caveat: the two companies use different accounting methods. OpenAI's numbers come from investor documents, while Anthropic's are from its IPO filing, so the figures aren't perfectly comparable. OpenAI's ~$50 billion annualized run rate also excludes gross partner revenue that was once folded into a widely cited $68 billion figure.


## The Funding Round Falls Short


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) is finalizing a funding round that values it at **$1.25 trillion** — below the $1.4 trillion it initially sought. The company has closed an initial **$11 billion** tranche,[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/openai-secures-11-billion-funding-125-trillion-valuation-bloomberg-news-reports-2026-11-06/) reported, out of a round that was once targeted at up to $30 billion but is now expected to land closer to **$20 billion** , per[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/06/openai-reportedly-raises-an-additional-11-billion-at-a-1-25-trillion-valuation/) .


Meanwhile[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) is targeting a **$1.4 trillion valuation** in an IPO that's already oversubscribed. OpenAI confidentially filed for its own IPO in June 2026 but has told employees it won't go public until **2027** . The valuation gap — and the efficiency gap — will shape how public markets price both companies.


## What This Means for Builders


For developers, the numbers confirm what the product roadmaps already hinted at:[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's growth now depends on **coding agents, security tooling, and AI assistants sold into the enterprise** — not just consumer ChatGPT subscriptions. Friar's reference to Coding and Cyber products signals where OpenAI will keep investing, which matters if you're building on top of those APIs.


The compute math also matters. OpenAI is spending billions to lock up Oracle, Azure, and AWS capacity, which means **API capacity and pricing will stay tied to how fast that compute comes online** . If demand keeps outstripping supply, builders should expect continued pressure on pricing and rate limits even as the models get cheaper to run.


- **Enterprise doubled QoQ** Now 50% of OpenAI's revenue — the growth engine is coding and agent products, not consumer chat


- **Loss per dollar: $1.09** Down from $1.50 in Q2 — efficiency improving, but still losing money on every dollar


- **Anthropic: $17B revenue, $567M loss** The efficiency gap is widening as Anthropic heads to IPO at $1.4T


- **Funding round fell short** $1.25T valuation, $11B closed of a ~$20B target, down from $30B
